conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I’m Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during your stay. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, Doctor. I’ve had a fever and really bad diarrhea for a few days. My stomach hurts like a volcano—comes and goes but always there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. Any nausea or vomiting?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No vomiting. But food just runs through me. I haven’t eaten much in two days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: And any pain when you urinate or blood in your urine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I don’t think so. No burning or pain down there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I know you were on Augmentin a while back for a bite wound. Did the diarrhea start then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it started while I was on that antibiotic. But it stopped after I finished it. Then came back about a week ago with the fever.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. We’re going to run some tests to figure out what’s going on. We’ve already checked your stool for C. diff, and it came back negative.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh, good. I was worried it might be that again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also did a chest X-ray to make sure you don’t have pneumonia, especially since you’re on immunosuppressants. The X-ray looks clear.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. My lungs feel okay.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re also checking your urine. Sometimes infections can cause symptoms like fever and belly pain, especially in transplant patients.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I didn’t think of that. But my transplant kidney doesn’t hurt.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s good. We’ll also do an ultrasound of your transplanted kidney tomorrow to make sure everything looks normal.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. Your urine culture came back. You have E. coli, which is causing a bladder infection—what we call a complicated UTI because of your transplant.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh no. Is that serious?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It can be, especially with your medical history. But we caught it early. The bacteria are sensitive to antibiotics, so we’re treating it effectively.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So the diarrhea is from the bladder infection?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, sometimes infections like this can cause GI symptoms, especially in people on immunosuppressants. Your stool tests were all negative—no C. diff, no parasites, no other bacteria.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. I was so worried it was my gut again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We also got your kidney ultrasound back. It looks completely normal—good blood flow, no swelling or blockage. Your transplant is doing well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. That’s a huge relief.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve started you on IV antibiotics—ceftriaxone. Once you’re stable, we’ll switch you to an oral antibiotic to finish a full 14-day course.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need to take it at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll send you home with cefpodoxime. It’s important to finish the whole course, even if you feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’ve learned my lesson with antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. We also checked your CMV and other viruses—those came back negative, so we don’t think a virus is causing this.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m glad. I’ve had enough infections lately.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Morning. How are you feeling today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Better. No fever last night, and the stomach pain is much milder.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Your labs today show your white blood cell count is coming down, which means the infection is responding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my kidney numbers?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your creatinine is 1.3, which is at your baseline. We held your furosemide while you were sick, but we can restart it tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my other meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ve been taking your tacrolimus and sirolimus the whole time. Levels are stable. All your other home meds will continue as before.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news—we’re discharging you today. You’ve improved a lot.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s wonderful. What do I need to do at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Finish the cefpodoxime for 14 days. Watch for fever, pain, or diarrhea returning. Stay hydrated and try to eat small, bland meals.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your primary doctor and nephrologist will follow up. Call us if you develop any new symptoms or can’t keep fluids down.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Doctor. I feel much better already.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and get some rest at home.
